title: Keep the stack when the Operator goes away

scenes.heading: Remove the controller or the stack?
scenes.sub: The live releases have their own lifecycle.
voice: You need to remove or replace the controller, while the cluster's GPU workloads keep running.
The Operator's deletion policy determines what happens to the releases it coordinates.

scenes.heading: Orphan keeps the releases in place
scenes.sub: Apps reconcile while the registry is reachable.
voice: Under the default orphan policy, deleting the runtime leaves its Argo CD Applications in place.
They keep reconciling the last state while they can reach their chart registry.

scenes.heading: Adopt the orphaned Applications
scenes.sub: A new runtime names the previous owner.
voice: When a new runtime takes over, identify the old runtime whose Applications it should adopt.
The Operator verifies those Applications and requires approval before it changes their ownership.

scenes.heading: Use Delete when teardown is intended
scenes.sub: Approved releases come down in order.
voice: Use the delete policy when you intend to remove the releases.
After approval, the removal rollout tears down dependent releases before the components they use.

viewer: Operators replacing or removing the controller
payoff: See how retaining releases differs from approved removal, including when explicit adoption is needed.
